references.text: The Lord repeats the description of Israel as a stiff-necked people, and this prevents His presence among them
The Lord again calls Israel a stiff-necked people and warns of the consequences
Moses asks for forgiveness for the people and acknowledges that they are a stiff-necked people
Moses reminds Israel that they are a stiff-necked people
The Lord speaks to Moses and uses the same expression regarding Israel's stubbornness
Israel is urged to circumcise their hearts and no longer be stiff-necked
Moses describes Israel's rebellion and stubbornness
Israel made their necks stiff like their fathers and refused to trust in the Lord
The Levites' prayer reminds that the fathers were stiff-necked and did not obey God's commands
Refers directly to the incident of the golden calf and the people's stubbornness
Stephen calls the Jews a stiff-necked people who always resist the Holy Spirit, using the same language as in the Old Testament
